03-incomplete-node-name-fallback.atd.note: "met" is not registered — Unknown Command Fallback (Inline Spec §6), not an error.

04-bare-at-symbol-fallback.atd.note: Bare "@" and "@GitHub" both fall back to plain text (Inline Spec §2/§6).

05-stray-closing-bracket-fallback.atd.note: An unpaired "]" at the document root is lenient, not Strict-Mode-checked — see parseImplicitParagraph.

16-unclosed-raw-domain-silent-swallow.at.note: KNOWN LIMITATION: no EOF check in the raw-content scanner — it silently consumes to end of file instead of erroring. See tests/README.md.

17-unknown-node-in-comma-list.atd.messageContains: only plain text and inline formatting
17-unknown-node-in-comma-list.atd.note: @card isn't in registry.ts's cell-formatting allowlist (unlike @bold/@link/etc.) — Strict Mode throws rather than silently dropping it.

18-svg-node-valid.atd.note: @svg is a raw pass-through node (like @mermaid) — embedded <svg> markup parses as opaque raw content, not escaped text.

19-color-node-valid.atd.note: @color{#ff0000}[...] — inline node for literal text color, distinct from @mark's background highlight. Shares @mark's {styles} slot (optional, same named tokens or hex), just resolves named tokens through its own darker palette.

20-list-no-dash-valid.atd.note: @list items no longer require a leading "- " — any non-empty line is an item (Structural-Blocks.md §5 List).

21-list-ordered-valid.atd.note: @list(ordered)[...] — renders as <ol> instead of the default bullet <ul>.

22-list-ordered-manual-marker-valid.atd.note: A leading "N. "/"N)" on an item inside @list(ordered) is captured as an explicit marker (<li value="N">), letting the numbering jump/resume.

23-list-nested-valid.atd.note: A line holding only a nested @list[...] is folded into the previous item instead of becoming a sibling item, producing a real nested <ul>/<ol>.

24-list-ordered-no-dash-valid.atd.note: @list(ordered) doesn't require a leading "- " either — same dash-optional rule as plain @list (20-list-no-dash-valid.atd), just rendered as <ol>.

25-table-cell-inline-formatting-valid.at.note: @table cells now accept a curated set of inline formatting nodes (registry.ts's isCellAllowedNode) — @bold, @link, @n all parse as real nodes instead of throwing.

26-color-old-paren-disabled.atd.messageContains: no longer accepts a parenthesized value
26-color-old-paren-disabled.atd.note: @color(#hex) was retired when @color moved to sharing @mark's {styles} slot — the old paren form is now a hard error instead of silently discarding the value.

27-table-cell-raw-family-paren-valid.atd.note: @code(js)[...] inside a table cell — regression test for a bug where parseInlineCellList() only consumed the NODE token before expecting RAW, so a raw-family node with a paren (like @code's language tag) threw a misleading 'expects a content slot' error. @raw[...] (no paren) alongside it confirms the pre-existing no-paren raw-family flattening still works.

28-styles-slot-on-unstyled-node.atd.note: The Lexer tokenizes "{...}" after any node name, so a {styles} slot on a node whose grammar defines none (@heading here) used to be parsed and then silently dropped. Only nodes with a `styles` StyleSet in registry.ts accept one.

29-table-row-column-count-mismatch.atd.messageContains: every row must match the column count exactly
29-table-row-column-count-mismatch.atd.note: A thousands-separator comma ("80,000") silently split one cell into two, so the row parses clean at 4 cells against @cols's 2 columns. Previously accepted silently (the cells just shifted); now flagged instead of rendering misaligned columns.

30-hex-node-valid.atd.note: v0.1.2 (README.md §A-3) — @hex[#3366ff] displays a color swatch + its own literal code, distinct from @color{#hex}[...] which recolors other text. Both "#RGB" and "#RRGGBB" forms are accepted.

31-hex-node-invalid-format.atd.messageContains: must be a "#RGB" or "#RRGGBB" color code
31-hex-node-invalid-format.atd.note: @hex's content is restricted (like @kbd's `key`, but further constrained to an actual hex color) — a named color word isn't valid content for it.

32-spoiler-node-valid.atd.note: v0.1.2 (README.md §A-2) — @spoiler is a nestable inline node (unlike @kbd/@hex's restricted text), so @spoiler[@bold[...]] parses as a real nested node, not flattened text.

33-img-align-float-valid.atd.note: v0.1.2 (README.md §A-1) — "align=float-left" is a new recognized @img option value alongside the existing left/center/right.

34-img-align-unrecognized-value.atd.note: "align=middle" isn't a recognized value — flagged as a warning-severity diagnostic (parser.diagnostics still records it), not an error, since the document still renders something reasonable either way. run-tests.ts's shouldThrow only counts error-severity diagnostics, so this case is expected to parse clean by that measure.

35-card-style-token-unrecognized.atd.note: @card{blue} — Card Style v1 only accepts "#RRGGBB" or "radius-N"; a named color token like @mark's {styles} accepts was previously accepted and silently dropped by the renderer with no signal anywhere. Message wording comes from diagnoseUnknownStyleTokens's shared allowedDesc string ("#RRGGBB" or "radius-N").

36-defn-non-integer-id.atd.note: @defn(note-a) — @fn[...] only ever accepts an integer reference, so a non-numeric @defn id can never actually be linked to from anywhere; previously accepted silently.

37-img-align-bare-keyword-valid.atd.note: registry.ts's parseImgOptions() recognizes a bare comma item matching a known align value (e.g. "float-left") without the "align=" key — the vocabulary is closed, so it's unambiguous. "align=float-left" still works too; this is purely an additive shorthand, not a replacement.

38-table-pipe-delimiter-valid.atd.note: v0.1.2 (README.md §3.4/§3.5) — @cols/@data using "|" instead of "," once a "|" appears anywhere at depth 0. Exercises the doc's own worked example in one case: a comma inside a pipe-delimited cell stays literal ("陳大文, 林美華"), @span(2) makes a 2-cell row satisfy 3 columns, and a genuinely empty MIDDLE cell ("||資料工程小組") stays a real empty column since edge-stripping only ever touches the first/last cell of a row, not a middle one.

39-table-pipe-edge-leniency-valid.atd.note: A leading and/or trailing "|" is decorative and stripped independently per edge — "[|a|b|]", "[1|2|]", and "[|1|2]" (2, 2, and 2 cells respectively) all parse the same as "[a|b]"/"[1|2]". There's no way to represent a genuinely empty first/last column via an edge "|" any more.

40-span-outside-table.atd.messageContains: may only appear directly inside `@data row`
40-span-outside-table.atd.note: @span used outside a table cell — restrictedTo (registry.ts) rejects it the same way @tab is rejected outside @tabs.

41-span-non-integer-count.atd.note: @span(two) — registry.ts's parseSpanCount() only accepts a plain positive integer; falls back to counting as width-1 for the row/@cols check (not re-flagged there too) rather than double-reporting the same root cause two ways.

42-table-pipe-row-mismatch.atd.note: A pipe-delimited row with a genuine width mismatch (no @span involved) is still flagged, same as the legacy comma-delimited check (case 29) — the new syntax doesn't relax the row/@cols invariant.
